neighbours.label: contexts where waste or pollutants are released into the environment (just before discharge/dump/vent into)
fire: The mill was found to discharge untreated chemicals into the creek.
For years the city let raw sewage flow straight into the harbor.
Gas heaters must vent their fumes to the outside of the building.
Ships often pump oily bilge water overboard once they leave port.
Residents complained that trucks were dumping garbage in the empty lot.
The plant releases thousands of tons of sulfur dioxide into the air each year.
Farm runoff carries manure and fertilizer into nearby streams.
Illegal miners pour mercury into the river while washing gold.
quiet: The mill was found to employ untrained workers at the creek.
For years the city let tourists walk straight into the harbor.
Gas heaters must be inspected by a technician every winter.
Ships often take on fresh supplies once they reach port.
Residents complained that trucks were parking in the empty lot.
The plant produces thousands of tons of steel for export each year.
Farm workers carry hay and tools to the nearby barns.
Local miners sell gold in the town after a long week.
